surface_reconstruction.description: Recover the albedo and depth maps of surface-like hidden objects from noisy confocal transients at the paper's Zaragoza acquisition scale (1 m x 1 m relay wall, 256 x 256 scan points, 3 mm of photon path per time bin), plus 384 x 384 (train) and 512 x 512 (hidden test) scans. Scores are means over the scenes of the split (6 visible train scenes, 12 hidden test scenes rendered at test time). The paper's headline quality claim is the lowest depth MAE on the Zaragoza bunny among direct methods (Fig. 5) while keeping image quality comparable to volumetric methods (Figs. 4, 6). A run that fails any constraint (missing/invalid output, non-finite or out-of-range values, wrong shape, memory budget, time limit, or the task-success gates) receives bounded failure values on every metric: the best-constant depth error, zero correlation, the empty-image PSNR and the full memory budget.

depth_mae_cm.description: Mean absolute depth error (cm) over wall pixels fully covered by an object, averaged over scenes. Task-success gate: must be at most half of the error of the best constant-depth answer.

albedo_ncc.description: Pearson correlation between the predicted and true albedo maps over all wall pixels (scale- and offset-invariant: albedo is only recoverable up to a global factor), averaged over scenes. Task-success gate: at least 0.2.

albedo_psnr_db.description: PSNR (dB) of the predicted albedo after the least-squares global scale fit against the true albedo normalised to peak 1, averaged over scenes. Never below the PSNR of an empty image, which is the failure value.

surface_reconstruction._paper_note: The _paper_* entries are the paper's Fig. 5 depth MAE on the simulated Zaragoza Stanford bunny (256 x 256 scan, 1 m x 1 m wall, s = 0.02). This gym uses the same acquisition scale but procedurally generated noisy scenes with ground truth (the public Zaragoza files have no 2D ground-truth maps), so those numbers are kept for context and are not targets.

working_memory.description: Peak resident memory (MB) of the method's process tree, measured by the evaluator from the operating system while the method reconstructs each scene; the score is the maximum over the split's scenes, so it is set by the largest scan (384 x 384 train, 512 x 512 hidden test). The paper's efficiency claim is that working memory stays far below volumetric methods (under 50 MB vs over 13 GB on Zaragoza). Runs whose memory exceeds the 256 MB budget on any scene are failed (the uint16 histogram of a 512 x 512 x 512 scan alone is 256 MB).

peak_memory_mb.description: Maximum over scenes of the peak resident memory (MB) of the method's process tree, measured by the evaluator from /proc (per-process high-water mark and summed tree RSS; includes interpreter, libraries and touched memory-mapped pages), reported at 4 MB resolution because identical runs vary by about 1 MB. Failure value: the 256 MB budget.

working_memory._paper_note: Paper values: the Quasi-Fresnel reconstruction needs 'less than 50 MB' (a loose MATLAB-profiling upper bound) on Zaragoza instances, previous volumetric methods 'over 13.105 GB'. Measured here as Python process peak RSS on 384-512 scans, so the numbers are context, not targets.
